profiles._comment_opening_loadout: THE TURN-ONE OUTFITTING WINDOW, AND THE ONLY SOURCE OF OPENING GEAR AND MATERIAL. A spawning band owns NOTHING - equipment.json ships `start_stock_fraction: 0.0` and no material declares a start stock any more - so the player composes the opening loadout after seeing the generated map, and anything unspent when the first turn advances is forfeited. ONE BUDGET, AND IT IS NOT CONFIGURED HERE: the band's CARRY, its working-age hands x expedition_config.json carry.per_worker_carry (17 x 8.0 = 136 on the shipped 30-person band). Kits and materials are spent from it in one load currency - a kit weighs the items it expands to x carry.item_carry_weight, a material unit weighs carry.material_carry_weight - and the band's own larder does NOT count against it, because it has not walked anywhere. A retuned band size, working share or pack moves the budget with no edit here. `pickable_materials` is the pick list the client draws, in the order it draws them; a material absent from it cannot be bought at any price, which is how the three luxury crops and `hurdles` stay off a list nobody would spend on. `material_defaults` and `kit_defaults` are the DEFAULT OUTFIT the sim applies to every band the moment it exists - the allocation the window opens on, which the player is free to revise - and must name only pickable materials and roster kits that carry something. There is no sum check: the budget is the band's own carry, which does not exist at load, so the defaults are FITTED PROPORTIONALLY (kits and materials together, floored, remainder unspent) to whatever budget the band turned out to have, with a warn on the opening band when it binds. The shipped 4/4/4 kits (20 items) + 28 material units = 48 against 136 never binds on the opening band; a splinter's smaller budget is routinely fitted. Every picked unit arrives at the MIDDLE of the band table on every axis it declares (OPENING_MATERIAL_READING): what the band scavenged before setting out is unremarkable.
